transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you and what brings you in today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because things just haven't been right. Since... since my grandson was killed. 

My daughter, she... she can sit right beside me, holding my hand, and I know I love her. I know I do. But I just... I cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all anymore. I just don't feel it.
Have you found that you don't take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other activities?
No... not really. I just... I mostly just sit. I don't do much of anything these days.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of persistent low mood, lack of pleasure, and psychomotor retardation following a significant bereavement supports major depressive disorder, either single or recurrent episode, severe without psychotic features. Adjustment disorder and PTSD were ruled out due to the duration and severity of symptoms.
